sum: Vale's finance chief Marcelo Bacci said on Friday, October 30, that the miner is unlikely to pay an extraordinary dividend in 2026, according to Reuters. The statement followed Vale's third-quarter results on Thursday, October 29, and shifts the near-term capital-return focus toward balance-sheet discipline.

Management cited geopolitical uncertainty surrounding 2027 and said Vale preferred to retain more cash and maintain lower indebtedness. The company paid 1.7 billion US dollars in dividends and interest on capital during the third quarter, but investors should not expect that distribution level to be supplemented by a special payout this year.

The decision does not remove shareholder returns from the discussion. Management has described share repurchases as attractive at current prices, although no buyback size or timing was announced. That leaves the capital-allocation outlook less certain than a regular dividend schedule alone would suggest.

Vale expects 2026 iron ore output at the lower end of its 335 million to 345 million tonne guidance range. Management indicated that 2027 iron ore guidance should not differ substantially from this year's range, with the details scheduled for the Vale Day investor meeting on Tuesday, December 1.

The update comes after third-quarter net income fell 53 percent year over year while revenue increased 2 percent. Lower iron ore prices and higher fuel and freight costs pressured profitability, while copper and nickel operations provided operational support. For investors, the December meeting should clarify whether production stability can offset weaker iron ore economics.

Marcus Blackmore And The Vitamins Empire Built On Stock
sum: Brookvale, on Sydney’s northern beaches, is not where you’d expect a listed pharmaceutical company’s roots to sit. But that’s where Maurice Blackmore set up a naturopathy clinic in the 1930s, selling herbal remedies out the back to patients who trusted him more than their doctors. His son Marcus joined the business in 1964, not as an heir with a strategy, but as a 21-year-old who’d failed his first attempt at university and needed somewhere to be useful. Sixty years later the company that grew from that shopfront, Blackmores, carries a market value that at its peak topped $2 billion. The story in between is less about vision and more about someone who stuck around long enough to get the timing right, twice.

I’ve spent a fair bit of time this year going back through old annual reports from companies that are still household names, and Blackmores is one of the stranger ones. It survived the 1970s as a fringe operation selling fish oil and wheatgerm to a market that barely existed. It survived a near-death stock crisis in the early 2000s that almost nobody outside the industry remembers now. And it survived, more recently, a collapse in Chinese demand that wiped out the better part of its share price inside eighteen months. None of that reads like genius. It reads like a business that kept showing up.

Maurice Blackmore was, by most accounts, a difficult man to work for and an even harder one to satisfy. He ran his clinic on a conviction that mainstream medicine had abandoned nutrition, and he built a small range of supplements to back that conviction up. When Marcus came into the business there was no grand plan for scale. The company incorporated formally in 1938 and limped along as a modest supplier to health food shops for decades, the kind of operation that existed because its founder believed in it, not because the market was clamouring for it.

What changed things wasn’t a single breakthrough product. It was distribution. Marcus Blackmore understood earlier than most in the natural health sector that pharmacies, not health food shops, were where the volume lived. Getting Blackmores products onto pharmacy shelves alongside Panadol and Codral gave the brand a legitimacy the industry hadn’t had before.

items.t: Vale stock: Cash flow supports outlook after Q3 earnings squeeze
sum: Vale released its third-quarter 2026 results on Thursday, October 29, with weaker iron ore economics weighing on profitability while copper and nickel operations provided support. The company's official Q3 2026 results release also added detail on costs, cash flow and metal-price realization.

Vale reported pro forma EBITDA of 3.5 billion US dollars for the quarter, down 20 percent from a year earlier and 14 percent from the previous quarter. The company attributed the decline mainly to lower realized iron ore fines prices, appreciation of the Brazilian real and higher bunker costs.

The average realized iron ore fines price fell to 85.1 US dollars per tonne, while iron ore C1 cash cost rose to 23.1 US dollars per tonne. All-in costs reached 60.4 US dollars per tonne, reflecting additional pressure from freight expenses.

Vale generated recurring free cash flow of 1.4 billion US dollars and total free cash flow of 2.2 billion US dollars in the quarter. Expanded net debt stood at 16.4 billion US dollars, 0.2 billion US dollars lower than in the previous quarter, as cash generation helped offset weaker EBITDA.

Iron ore sales increased 0.3 percent despite a 6 percent production decline. Copper sales fell 4 percent during the planned Sossego SAG mill rebuild, while nickel sales rose 16.1 percent. Vale reaffirmed its 2026 production guidance and expects copper and nickel output in the upper half of their respective ranges.

The company maintained its iron ore production guidance of 335 million to 345 million tonnes and expects full-year capital spending toward the lower end of its 5.4 billion to 5.7 billion US dollar range. Approval of the Salobo coarse particle flotation project adds a longer-term copper growth option based on existing infrastructure.

Vale stock holds 2026 guidance as iron ore weighs on Q3
sum: Vale's third-quarter results showed a sharp split across its metals portfolio. Iron ore earnings came under pressure from lower realized prices and higher external costs, while copper and nickel operations gained momentum. The company kept its 2026 production guidance intact.

In its 3Q26 Quarterly Results, Vale reported Proforma EBITDA of 3.5 billion US dollars for the July-to-September period, down 20 percent from a year earlier and 14 percent from the second quarter. The decline was mainly linked to weaker iron ore fines prices, a stronger Brazilian real and higher bunker costs.

The average realized iron ore fines price fell 10 percent year over year and quarter over quarter to 85.1 US dollars per tonne. Iron ore C1 cash costs rose 12 percent year over year to 23.1 US dollars per tonne, while all-in costs climbed 21 percent to 60.4 US dollars per tonne.

Iron ore production dropped 6 percent year over year, but sales increased 0.3 percent as Vale sold inventory accumulated in earlier periods. Pellet production rose 7 percent. The company attributed the lower iron ore output mainly to reduced run-of-mine availability at Serra Norte, partly offset by a quarterly production record at Serra Sul and additional volumes from the Capanema and Vargem Grande projects.

Vale Base Metals provided a counterweight. Realized copper prices increased to 15,314 US dollars per tonne, up 56 percent year over year, while nickel sales rose 16.1 percent. Copper sales were lower because of the planned Sossego SAG mill rebuild, but management said copper and nickel production remained on track for the upper half of their 2026 guidance ranges.

CEO Gustavo Pimenta said the company's freight strategy and hedging program helped protect margins in a dynamic market. Vale also highlighted the Serra Sul +20 project and the Compact Crushing project, which are intended to improve S11D performance. The company said October daily production at Serra Norte was already 15 percent higher, supporting its expectation of a stronger finish to the year.

Vale reaffirmed all 2026 production targets and said it remained confident of reaching the lower end of its iron ore guidance. Full-year capital expenditure is expected near the lower end of the 5.4 billion to 5.7 billion US dollar range.

sum: Brazilian stocks plunged after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a fourth term in Sunday's presidential runoff, defeating right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro and overturning market expectations of a shift toward more conservative economic policies.
The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF EWZ fell more than 27% in premarket trading on Monday as investors unwound positions built around a potential Bolsonaro victory.

Shares of oil major Petróleo Brasileiro S.A. - Petrobras PBR also tumbled, while banking stocks including Itaú Unibanco Holding S.A. ITUB and Banco Bradesco S.A. BBD came under heavy selling pressure.

The selloff followed a rally in Brazilian assets after Bolsonaro unexpectedly led the first round of voting earlier this month. Investors had anticipated that a change in political leadership could bring tighter fiscal policies, corporate tax reform and potential privatizations, helping contain government debt and eventually lower borrowing costs.

The strengthening Brazilian real had also supported sentiment by potentially easing inflationary pressures and attracting foreign capital. Lula's victory reversed those expectations, while Bolsonaro's refusal to concede and his challenge to the election result added to political uncertainty.

Rio Tinto (RIO) experienced a decline today, largely influenced by a significant drop in iron ore prices and recent analyst downgrades.

Iron ore prices fell to their lowest level since mid-April on June 3, with the benchmark July iron ore contract on the Singapore Exchange decreasing due to weakening steel demand in China, seasonal factors, and shrinking profit margins for steel producers. The most actively traded iron ore contract on the Dalian Commodity Exchange also saw a decline. As a major producer of iron ore, Rio Tinto's revenue and profitability are directly impacted by these price movements.

Compounding the pressure, RBC Capital downgraded Rio Tinto's stock rating to "Underperform" from "Sector Perform." This adjustment was made due to valuation concerns and the firm's expectation of continued weakness in iron ore prices, forecasting a decline to $85 per tonne by the end of 2027. Similarly, BofA Securities also downgraded Rio Tinto's stock from Buy to Neutral, citing valuation and macroeconomic factors, including China's credit impulse and global risks related to oil markets. These revised analyst outlooks, highlighting concerns about the stock's current valuation despite a strong performance over the past year, have likely contributed to negative investor sentiment.

Facts of Celtic managerial appointment
sum: There are a few irrefutable facts concerning the appointment of Celtic’s permanent manager. The most obvious is that recent assertions in the media are contradictory and therefore cannot all be true. The same people who brought you, “Martin will be appointed tomorrow”, also brought you “Robbie will be interviewed tonight”.

The second obvious fact is that Celtic are doing their business without keeping the media in the loop. No one is getting the tip-off on what’s going on, not a single scribe. The result of this will not be a discussion on the finer points of Celtic’s glorious double win, there are only so many days that sells. Speculation sells better than anything in the business, be it players or managers, and we are in peak Speculation Season right now. If you are in the news business and you are not selling Speculation, take a good look at yourself!

Beyond these obvious truths, the everyday process of recruitment continues. Agents will have been pitching to Celtic since the day Wilfried wilted. Celtic (should) build relationships with agents, and I know for a fact that they have interviewed managerial candidates in the past as a courtesy to the agent. That does not mean they were seriously considered.

Leaks also happen, but try picking the genuine ones from the fakes and you are a better man than me. Information can leak, only for it to quickly become bad information. Davie Provan once reported live on radio that Martin O’Neill had agreed to leave Celtic for Leeds United. It didn’t happen, Provan was on the receiving end of a barrage of abuse from Celtic fans, upset at his undermining the club during a crucial season (2002-03). Years later, we learned Provan was right, but Martin changed his mind.

There are human practicalities as well. The only thing Martin was clear about at the end of the season, was that he was unclear on whether or not he wanted the job. If he has been offered the job (hmmmm), is he entitled to consider the prospect over a holiday? Dermot Dermond gave him 10 minutes to consider the interim position in October, the situation is considerably different now.
You know as much as I do, and we both know as much as anyone else who is reporting on the subject.

sum: VALE S.A VALE and Rio Tinto RIO rank among the world's largest iron ore producers and diversified miners, making them direct competitors in the global metals and mining sector.

Apart from iron ore, Vale S.A also produces nickel, copper and cobalt, as well as by-products, such as gold, silver, platinum group metals, and other precious metals. Headquartered in Brazil, VALE has a market capitalization of around $65 billion.

Headquartered in London, the UK, Rio Tinto has a market capitalization of $141 billion. It engages in iron ore mining, alumina refining, smelting and recycling, as well as mining and processing of lithium. It also mines copper, gold, silver, molybdenum and other by-products.

Both are expected to play a central role in the global supply of essential commodities such as iron ore, copper and other minerals critical to industrial and economic development. Vale reported revenues of $38 billion in 2025, up 1% year over year. Adjusted earnings per share were $1.82, up 15%, supported by ongoing cost discipline. Iron ore and copper output reached the highest levels since 2018, while nickel production was the strongest since 2022.

Vale targets iron ore production capacity at 335-345 Mt in 2026 and plans to take it up to 360 Mt by 2030. The Vargem Grande 1 (VGR1) project and the Capanema Maximization project are anticipated to play a key role in attaining these targets, each expected to add about 15 Mtpy of capacity. Additional initiatives, including Compact Crushing at S11D and Serra Sul, are also set to boost capacity from the second half of 2026.

Vale is also investing heavily in the base metals business to benefit from the global energy transition. In 2026, Vale's copper production is expected to be between 350 kt and 380 kt. Copper production is expected to reach 420-500 kt as of 2030 and 700 kt by 2035.

BHP has a market capitalization of $165 billion, while VALE has a market capitalization of $66 billion.
For investors interested in this space, let's analyze which stock is better positioned for upside, BHP or Vale. A closer look at their fundamentals, growth drivers and key risks can offer clarity.

BHP produced a record 263 Mt of iron ore in fiscal 2025, within its guided 255-265.5 Mt and up 1% year over year. Production at Western Australia Iron Ore (WAIO) was a record of 257 Mt (290 Mt on a 100% basis). WAIO has been the lowest-cost iron ore producer globally for more than four years.

The upside continued in the first half of fiscal 2026 with iron ore production increasing 2% year over year to 134 Mt. WAIO reported a record first half production of 130 Mt, aided by strong supply-chain performance.

For fiscal 2026, BHP continues to expect iron ore production of 258-269 Mt. WAIO's output is likely to be 251-262 Mt (284-296 Mt on a 100% basis). This factors in the planned renewal of Car Dumper 3 (CD3) and the ongoing tie-in activities for Rail Technology Program 1 (RTP1).

BHP continues to reshape its portfolio toward commodities such as copper and potash, allocating nearly 70% of its medium-term capital expenditure to these areas. This strategy positions the company to benefit from decarbonization, electrification, population growth and rising living standards in emerging markets.

Savannah Reveals Her Voice and When She’s Returning to TODAY After Vocal Surgery
sum: Savannah Guthrie will soon make her way back to TODAY after resting up from a vocal cord surgery she had underwent late last year.
On Jan. 20, the TODAY co-anchor video called into the show to share the good news with Craig Melvin, Jenna Bush Hager, Al Roker, Carson Daly and Sheinelle Jones.
She later revealed she will return briefly to TODAY on Friday, Jan. 23, to share with viewers her health journey before she officially returns to the anchor desk on Monday, Jan. 26.

When Savannah shared in late December that she would have surgery on her vocal cords, she said she would be away from TODAY for a few weeks and would have to remain totally silent for some of her recovery.

In early January, she posted an update on Instagram, writing on a whiteboard that she is “all good” following her surgery. “Thanks for prayers and love,” her message also said. She continued to use that whiteboard to communicate with her kids.
In her video call on Jan. 20, Savannah told the TODAY team that she is still on vocal rest but she is allowed to talk five to 10 minutes every hour.

“I think the good news is that it worked,” she said of the surgery. “It’s kind of a slow recovery. You’re allowed to talk and then if you talk too much, which is a real risk for me, you feel it. So you have to really take it easy.”

items.t: New community repair hub opens in Abingdon
items.s: Vale of White Horse District Council
sum: People in Abingdon and neighbouring villages will benefit from a new community repair hub, Shed Space, which offers a space to refurbish bikes and household items as well as opportunities to make new friends and share skills.

Shed Space, opened at Ride Revolution Headquarters, on Saturday (10 January) with over 50 local people visiting. Visitors got hands-on repairing bikes and shared ideas for skills they’d like to learn, skills they could share and ideas of social activities they would like to see at Shed Space.

Run by Vale of White Horse District Council’s Active Communities team and supported by Abingdon and Witney College, Active Oxfordshire, UKSPF and local bike shop Pedal Power Cycles, Shed Space was opened following community feedback for a place to connect, support mental health, and share skills. The hub welcomes people to repair and make things, work on projects together and support one another, while encouraging sustainability and reducing waste.

Henry, who recently moved to Abingdon said: “I’m here today to meet new people, make friends and hopefully share my talents and skills with others. This sort of project is really helpful because it helps people like me come out of my shell and see what events and people the lovely area has to offer.”

Following its launch, Shed Space will initially operate on a fortnightly basis, with the day to be confirmed soon. Once fully established, the hub will open weekly, offering a programme of events, workshops, and activities.

Councillor Helen Pighills, Cabinet Member for Community Health and Wellbeing at Vale of White Horse District Council, said: “It’s really encouraging to see so many residents come along to the opening of Shed Space and getting involved from day one. This new hub will be a real asset for the community, giving people a place to share skills and connect with others.”

Councillor Robert Clegg, Cabinet Member for Environmental Services, Climate Action and Nature Recovery at Vale of White Horse District Council, said: “It’s fantastic to see a community hub like Shed Space open in Abingdon. It will bring people together, give residents the chance to learn new skills, and make a real difference for the environment by encouraging repair and reuse.”

Vale shares are trading above both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages, signaling a sustained bullish trend.

Vale recently stated that iron ore production for 2025 was around 335 Mt, at the higher end of its targeted 325-335 Mt. Copper output was around 370 kt in 2025, also meeting the high end of its targeted 340-370 kt. Nickel output was reported at 175 kt compared with the company's target of 160-175 kt.

The company has budgeted capital expenditure for the Iron Ore Solutions Business at $4 billion in 2026 and $3.9 billion from 2027 onward. The company plans to increase its iron ore production capacity to 335-345 Mt in 2026 and 360 Mt by 2030.

The Vargem Grande 1 (VGR1) project and the Capanema Maximization project are expected to play a key role in attaining these targets. The VGR1 project is expected to add 15 Mtpy (metric tons per year) of iron ore capacity, with 11 Mt targeted in 2026. Ramp up is expected to be concluded in the second half of 2026.

items.t: Walmart Stock Split Explained: Opportunity or Hype?
sum: The Walmart stock split must be viewed within the broader context of market structure and investor behaviour. In an era where retail participation has grown significantly and fractional trading has normalised lower entry points, a split is no longer essential. Yet it remains a powerful signalling tool.
When a company with the scale and maturity of Walmart executes a split, it is often interpreted as a strategic expression of confidence in future earnings visibility and operational resilience.
Institutional managers frequently note that splits in mega cap firms tend to coincide with periods of internal optimisation, competitive re positioning and structural investment.

For Walmart, the timing aligns with multi year commitments to logistics modernisation, wage enhancements and integrated store fulfilment. This makes the split relevant not only from a trading standpoint but also from a corporate strategy perspective.
A 3 for 1 split may appear simple, but the internal considerations that precede such actions are complex. Walmart's leadership historically avoids unnecessary financial engineering.
Therefore, the decision suggests that management sought a share structure that better reflects the company's diversified shareholder base while supporting long term capital market engagement.

From a liquidity perspective, the reduced per share price broadens participation among international retail investors who may face platform or minimum purchase constraints. It also improves share availability for employee stock programmes and may subtly enhance Walmart's attractiveness within retail focused ETFs that prefer lower weighted share prices for allocation mechanics.
